cnd15:1.5: Blessed One, tell me this as it really is.
cnd15:2.1: Hearing of the hero with no desire for sensual pleasures: having heard, listened, learned, retained, and recognized.
cnd15:2.2: Such is that Blessed One, perfected … a Buddha, a Blessed One—
cnd15:2.5: He is a hero because he is energetic, a hero because he is capable, a hero because he is powerful, a hero because he is able, a hero because he is brave; he is a hero because he is valiant, fearless, unshaken, unafraid, does not flee, has given up fear and dread, and is free of goosebumps.
cnd15:4.7: For the Buddha, the Blessed One, sensual pleasures as objects have been fully understood, and sensual pleasures as corruptions have been given up.
cnd15:4.8: Because sensual pleasures as objects have been fully understood and sensual pleasures as corruptions have been given up, the Blessed One does not desire sensual pleasures, does not long for them, does not yearn for them, and does not hanker for them.
cnd15:4.9: Those who desire sensual pleasures, long for them, yearn for them, and hanker for them are those who desire desires, those who are greedy in their greed, those who are percipient in their perceptions.
cnd15:4.10: The Blessed One does not desire sensual pleasures, does not long for them, does not yearn for them, and does not hanker for them.
cnd15:4.11: Therefore the Buddha is without desire, free of desire, with desire renounced, vomited out, released, abandoned, and let go; free of greed, with greed gone, renounced, vomited out, released, abandoned, and let go; without wishes, quenched, cooled, experiencing bliss, he lives with a self become divine—
cnd15:5.2: Iccā: this is a joining of words … the sequence of words—
cnd15:5.4: Venerable: this is a friendly word, a form of address expressing respect and deference, that is, venerable.
cnd15:5.5: Jatukaṇṇī: this is that brahmin’s clan name, his designation, appellation, description, and usage—
cnd15:6.2: Who has gone beyond the flood: one who has transcended, completely transcended, and passed beyond the flood—
cnd15:6.4: To ask: to ask, to question, to request, to invite, and to please.
cnd15:6.5: I have come to one without desire: to ask one who is without desire, free of desire, with desire renounced, vomited out, released, abandoned, and let go; free of greed, with greed gone, renounced, vomited out, released, abandoned, and let go; we have come, arrived, approached, reached you, and met with you—
cnd15:7.2: Peace: in one way, both peace and the state of peace are just the deathless extinguishment.
cnd15:7.3: That is the stilling of all activities, the letting go of all attachments, the ending of craving, fading away, cessation, extinguishment.
cnd15:7.5: “This state is peaceful, this state is sublime—that is, the stilling of all activities, the letting go of all attachments, the ending of craving, fading away, cessation, extinguishment.”
cnd15:7.6: Then, in another way, those things that lead to the attainment of peace, to the touching of peace, to the realization of peace, that is—
cnd15:7.7: the four kinds of mindfulness meditation, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven awakening factors, the noble eightfold path—
cnd15:7.9: The state of peace, the state of protection, the state of shelter, the state of refuge, the state of fearlessness, the state of the imperishable, the state of the deathless, the state of extinguishment: speak, explain, teach, assert, establish, clarify, analyze, disclose, and reveal.
cnd15:7.10: One with an innate eye: the eye is said to be the knowledge of omniscience.
cnd15:7.11: For the Buddha, the Blessed One, the eye and the state of being a victor arose together at the root of the Bodhi tree, in a single moment, neither earlier nor later; therefore the Buddha has an innate eye—
cnd15:8.1: Blessed One, tell me this as it really is: what is as it really is is said to be the deathless extinguishment … cessation, extinguishment.
cnd15:8.2: Blessed One: a term of respect … a designation based on realization, that is, Blessed One.
cnd15:10.1: For the Blessed One proceeds, having overcome sensual pleasures,
cnd15:10.4: explain the Dhamma that I may understand;
cnd15:11.1: For the Blessed One proceeds, having overcome sensual pleasures.
cnd15:11.2: Blessed One: a term of respect … a designation based on realization, that is, Blessed One.
cnd15:11.7: The Blessed One, having fully understood sensual pleasures as objects, having given up sensual pleasures as corruptions, and having overcome, subdued, overwhelmed, and exhausted them, lives, dwells, proceeds, keeps going, maintains, sustains, and carries on—
cnd15:12.1: Like the sun, blazing over the earth with its heat: ādicca is said to be sūriya, the sun.
cnd15:12.3: Just as the sun, blazing and endowed with heat, having overcome, subdued, overwhelmed, exhausted, and scorched the earth, having dispersed all the darkness in the sky, having cleared away the gloom, having shown the light, travels through the sky, the atmosphere, along the path of space; in the same way, the Blessed One, blazing with knowledge and endowed with the heat of knowledge, all the origin of choices …
cnd15:12.4: having dispelled the darkness of corruptions and the gloom of ignorance, having shown the light of knowledge, having fully understood sensual pleasures as objects, having given up sensual pleasures as corruptions, and having overcome, subdued, overwhelmed, exhausted, and crushed them, lives, dwells, proceeds, keeps going, maintains, sustains, and carries on—
cnd15:13.1: Of vast wisdom, to me of little wisdom: I am of little wisdom, of inferior wisdom, of base wisdom, of wretched wisdom.
cnd15:13.2: You, too, are of great wisdom, widespread wisdom, joyful wisdom, swift wisdom, sharp wisdom, penetrating wisdom.
cnd15:13.4: The Blessed One is endowed with wisdom as vast and extensive as the earth—
cnd15:14.1: Explain the Dhamma that I may understand.
cnd15:14.2: The Dhamma: the spiritual practice that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased, entirely full and pure; the four kinds of mindfulness meditation …
cnd15:14.3: extinguishment and the practice that leads to extinguishment: explain, teach, assert, establish, clarify, analyze, disclose, and reveal them.
cnd15:14.4: What I might understand: what I might know, understand, discern, acknowledge, penetrate, attain, touch, and realize—
cnd15:15.1: The giving up of rebirth and old age here: right here, the giving up, stilling, letting go, and calming of birth, old age, and death, the deathless extinguishment—
cnd15:18.7: That which is greed, intense greed … covetousness, avarice, the unskillful root.
cnd15:18.8: Dispel your avidity for sensual pleasures: dispel, completely dispel, give up, get rid of, eliminate, and obliterate your avidity for sensual pleasures—
cnd15:18.10: Jatukaṇṇī: the Blessed One addresses that brahmin by his clan name.
cnd15:18.11: Blessed One: this is a term of respect … a designation based on realization, that is, Blessed One—
cnd15:19.2: Renunciation: right practice, accordant practice, non-opposing practice, practice in line with the goal, practice in line with the teaching, fulfilling ethical conduct, guarding the sense doors, moderation in eating, dedication to wakefulness, mindfulness and situational awareness, the four kinds of mindfulness meditation, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven awakening factors, the noble eightfold path, and extinguishment and the practice that leads to extinguishment, to be seen as sanctuary, as protection, as shelter, as refuge, as a place of refuge, as fearless, as imperishable, as deathless, as extinguishment; having seen, observed, weighed up, examined, clarified, and made them clear—
cnd15:20.2: Grasped: held through craving or through views, adhered to, insisted on, attached to, and committed to.
cnd15:20.3: Or cast off: or to be let go, to be given up, to be dispelled, to be eliminated, to be obliterated—
cnd15:21.1: Let there be no possession found in you: the possession of greed, the possession of hate, the possession of delusion, the possession of conceit, the possession of views, the possession of corruptions, the possession of misconduct.
cnd15:21.2: Let this possession of yours not be found, not be found at all, not exist; give up, dispel, eliminate, and obliterate it—
cnd15:24.1: Let what came before wither away: regarding past activities, whatever corruptions might arise, dry up those corruptions, wither them, make them dry, thoroughly dry them out, make them seedless, give them up, dispel them, eliminate them, and obliterate them—
cnd15:24.3: Or else, whatever past choices of deeds have not yet ripened, dry up those choices of deeds, wither them, make them dry, thoroughly dry them out, make them seedless, give them up, dispel them, eliminate them, and obliterate them—
cnd15:25.1: Let there be no possession for you afterwards: afterwards is said to refer to future activities: the possession of greed, the possession of hate, the possession of delusion, the possession of conceit, the possession of views, the possession of corruptions, the possession of misconduct.
cnd15:25.2: Let this possession of yours not exist or come to be; do not give rise to it, do not originate it, do not produce it; give up, dispel, eliminate, and obliterate it—
cnd15:26.1: If you do not grasp at the middle: the middle is said to be the present: form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.
cnd15:26.2: You will not grasp, not seize, not adhere to, not delight in, not welcome, and not become attached to present conditions through the force of craving or the force of views.
cnd15:26.3: You will give up approval, welcoming, clinging, grasping, adherence, and insistence; you will dispel, eliminate, and obliterate them—
cnd15:27.1: You will live at peace: you will live at peace because greed has been calmed, because hate …
cnd15:27.2: because all unskillful choices have been calmed, settled, pacified, stilled, burned out, quenched, removed, and tranquilized, you will live, dwell, proceed, keep going, maintain, sustain, and carry on peaceful, serene, stilled, quenched, and tranquil—
cnd15:30.1: Entirely, for name and form, for one rid of avidity, brahmin.
cnd15:30.2: Entirely: wholly, totally, in every way, everything, without remainder, without exception; this is an expression of inclusiveness, that is, entirely.
cnd15:30.4: Form: the four great elements and the form derived from the four great elements.
cnd15:30.6: That which is greed, intense greed … covetousness, avarice, the unskillful root.
cnd15:30.7: Entirely for name and form, for one rid of avidity, brahmin: entirely for name and form, for one rid of avidity, with avidity gone, renounced, vomited out, released, abandoned, and let go; free of greed, with greed gone, renounced, vomited out, released, abandoned, and let go—
cnd15:30.8: entirely for name and form, for one rid of avidity, brahmin.
cnd15:31.3: the defilement of sensual desire, the defilement of continued existence, the defilement of views, the defilement of ignorance.
cnd15:31.5: Are not found: these defilements do not exist in him, are not present, are not found, are not obtained; they have been given up, completely cut off, stilled, calmed, incapable of arising again, and burned by the fire of knowledge—
cnd15:32.1: By which they might fall under the sway of Death: by whatever defilements he might come under the sway of Death, or come under the sway of dying, or come under the sway of Māra’s faction;
cnd15:32.2: those defilements do not exist in him, are not present, are not found, are not obtained; they have been given up, completely cut off, stilled, calmed, incapable of arising again, and burned by the fire of knowledge—
cnd15:34.2: Sir, the Blessed One is my Teacher, and I am a disciple.
